Code § 1946.2)","requirement":"After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential property for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without just cause stated in the written termination notice. If adult tenants are added before an existing tenant reaches 24 months, the rule applies only when all tenants have occupied for 12 months or more, or one or more tenants have occupied for 24 months or more. At-fault causes: nonpayment of rent, material lease breach, nuisance, waste, refusal to sign a lease extension, criminal activity, unlawful subletting, refusal of lawful owner entry, unlawful use, failure to vacate after employment ends, and failure to deliver possession after the tenant's own notice. No-fault causes: owner or family move-in (with conditions), withdrawal from the rental market, compliance with a government or court order or local ordinance requiring vacancy, and demolition or substantial remodel. For curable violations, the owner must first give notice and an opportunity to cure; if the violation is not cured, a three-day notice to quit may follow. For no-fault terminations the owner must, regardless of tenant income, either pay relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent, and must state this right in the notice. Owners must give tenants a prescribed notice of these rights, in at least 12-point type, in the lease or by written notice.
